what_it_does: The transport layer of C4ISR: it moves voice, data, video and machine-to-machine traffic between sensors, shooters, command posts and higher echelons when there is no fixed infrastructure and an adversary is jamming, geolocating and cyber-attacking the links. Concretely it comprises (1) tactical radios and waveforms (narrowband voice/data, wideband MANET such as TSM, Wave Relay and Silvus MN-MIMO), (2) beyond-line-of-sight transport (GEO/MEO/pLEO SATCOM incl. Starlink/Starshield, troposcatter, HF), (3) commercial cellular/5G bubbles, (4) gateways that translate between waveforms and data links (e.g., BACN, Link 16 gateways), (5) the IP/network layer that stitches these together (routing, encryption, SD-WAN style multi-path transport, PACE - primary/alternate/contingency/emergency - plan execution), and (6) NetOps: planning, monitoring, spectrum management and cyber defense of the tactical network. In 2025-2026 the U.S. Army explicitly separates a 'transport layer' from the data, integration and application layers of Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2), and the Space Force is buying a proliferated-LEO backbone (SDN Backbone / MILNET) as the space segment of that transport.

current_architecture.description: Army tactical transport today is a layered mix: Integrated Tactical Network (ITN) fielded to brigades since 2021 in capability sets combining program-of-record two-channel leader radios (AN/PRC-163, AN/PRC-148C) and manpacks with commercial MANET radios (Silvus StreamCaster, Persistent MPU5, TrellisWare TSM radios), a secure-but-unclassified enclave for Nett Warrior/ATAK, commercial LEO (Starlink/Starshield terminals) and GEO SATCOM, and unit-level routing/encryption. C2 Fix (2024-2026) is the bridge that simplified this for Transformation-in-Contact brigades; NGC2 (Anduril-led team for 4th ID, Lockheed-led team for 25th ID) defines a four-layer stack (transport, data, integration, application) with Persistent Wave Relay selected as network foundation for the NGC2 prototype (Oct 2025) and an $87.5M Army contract to Persistent (Feb 2026). Army plans a division-level NGC2 production ecosystem in FY27 and service-wide fielding by a tentative 2032. Above the tactical edge sit DISA/Space Force SATCOM (pLEO IDIQ, WGS, MUOS), SDA Transport Layer and the SpaceX-built SDN Backbone. Air: Link 16, BACN, ABMS gateways. Navy: CANES afloat network plus Overmatch software-defined networking on CSGs. NetOps is fragmented across vendor tools; UNO/TNO aims to unify.

current_architecture.security_domain: Mixed: SBU/unclassified commercial enclaves (ITN 'secure but unclassified'), SECRET (most PoR radios, Link 16), and TS/SCI for MILNET/NRO transport. Zero trust is an explicit AUNP 2.0 objective.
current_architecture.connectivity_dependency: This layer IS connectivity; upper layers (COP, fires, logistics) assume it. Commercial LEO dependence on a single provider (SpaceX ~97% of pLEO task orders) is itself a documented concentration risk (INFERENCE from Quilty and Breaking Defense reporting).
current_architecture.what_breaks_when_disconnected: Voice reverts to line-of-sight only; cloud-hosted C2 apps lose sync; PLI and chat stall; NetOps loses visibility; units fall back to manual PACE execution and runners. DIU ORIENT problem statement: swarms must keep operating as a system of systems in disrupted, low-bandwidth environments.

technical_difficulty.summary: Bimodal. Building radios/waveforms is very hard (RF front ends, MIMO/anti-jam DSP, NSA crypto certification, ruggedization, supply chain) and dominated by well-funded incumbents. Building the software above the radios - multi-path transport orchestration, PACE automation, NetOps visibility, DDIL data movement, gateway translation - is hard but tractable for strong distributed-systems/networking engineers, and is exactly where NGC2's 'transport-agnostic' direction and UNO create demand. The catch: software must work against proprietary radio APIs, on classified or CUI enclaves, and be proven in field exercises.
required_expertise: IP networking and routing in lossy/asymmetric links (OLSR/BATMAN-class MANET routing, QoS, multicast)
Distributed systems and eventual consistency for DDIL sync
Cryptography integration (IPsec, HAIPE, CSfC) and zero trust
Radio and SATCOM management APIs (SNMP/REST of Silvus, Persistent, Starlink, Kymeta)
Embedded Linux on SWaP-constrained edge boxes
RF fundamentals and spectrum management (important, not gating for software plays)
TAK/CoT and Link 16/VMF message handling for gateways
technical_difficulty.hardest_problem: Making a heterogeneous, multi-vendor, multi-orbit transport self-configure and fail over under jamming and movement without a signal soldier in the loop, while proving it through a security accreditation and a division-scale exercise - and doing so without radio vendors closing their APIs.
technical_difficulty.commodity_parts: COTS MANET radios, Starlink/Starshield terminals, 5G kits, rugged x86/ARM edge compute, open-source routing (FRR, BATMAN-adv), WireGuard/IPsec, TAK Server, MQTT/NATS, DTN implementations.

capital_intensity.proof_of_concept_usd: $100k-$400k for a software-only orchestration/NetOps/DDIL-sync prototype using 6-12 COTS radios and Starlink terminals in a lab or field test (assumes two founders, no clearance, unclassified data).
capital_intensity.credible_military_demo_usd: $1M-$4M: engineers with tactical network experience, export-controlled radio loans or purchases ($10k-$50k per Silvus/MPU5 node), participation in NetModX/Cyber Quest/Project Convergence-type events, initial cyber accreditation work, SBIR Phase I/II or DIU CSO funding.
capital_intensity.first_production_deployment_usd: $5M-$20M for software fielded to a division (ATO, CSfC/crypto integration, 24/7 support, training) ; $30M+ if any hardware radio/gateway product must be manufactured and certified.
capital_intensity.assumptions: Software-first play; hardware avoided; assumes SBIR/OTA non-dilutive funding covers demos; $250k founder capital reaches only proof of concept and initial customer discovery.

regulatory_access.prototype_with_commercial_unclassified_d: partly - orchestration, NetOps and sync prototypes can be built on unclassified COTS radios and Starlink, but realistic waveform behavior and PoR radio integration need CUI/ITAR technical data
regulatory_access.government_data_required: Not for MVP; needed later: radio management APIs (some ITAR-controlled), network topologies (CUI), exercise data.
regulatory_access.itar_ear: Military MANET radios and Type-1 radios are ITAR (USML XI) or EAR 5A001-class; pure networking software is often EAR (5D002 encryption) but any defense-specific integration can pull into ITAR. Requires specialist export-control review before any non-U.S.-person founder touches technical data.
regulatory_access.cui_likely: Yes - network plans, PACE plans, and exercise results are CUI at minimum.
regulatory_access.classified_integration_eventually: Yes - SECRET enclaves for PoR radios and Link 16; TS for MILNET/NRO transport.
regulatory_access.cleared_personnel_at_mvp: No for unclassified MVP; yes (SECRET) for anything touching PoR radios or NGC2 classified enclaves within 12-24 months.
regulatory_access.non_us_person_founder_note: An Indonesian founder who is not a U.S. person cannot access ITAR technical data or defense-article source code without an export license, and a facility clearance would trigger FOCI mitigation (possibly a proxy board or SSA) if that founder holds significant ownership/control. A German founder becoming a permanent resident becomes a 'U.S. person' for ITAR/EAR purposes on obtaining green card status but still needs citizenship for a personnel clearance. Workable structure: non-U.S.-person founder owns equity but is walled off from controlled technical data via a technology control plan; all of this needs specialist legal review - no definitive judgment here.

why_not_solved.explanation: Each MANET vendor (Silvus, Persistent, TrellisWare) owns its waveform, routing and management plane; cross-vendor orchestration threatens their lock-in, and PoR radios are Type-1 boxes with restricted interfaces.
Anything in the encrypted path needs NSA/CSfC approval and an ATO; waveform changes need lab and field certification; this slows software iteration to program timelines.
Army (PEO C3N), Space Force (CSCO/SDA), Navy (Overmatch), USAF (AFLCMC/ACC), DIU and SOCOM each buy transport separately; GAO-25-106454 documents CJADC2 isolation.

Affordable pLEO (Starlink since ~2021, MILNET 2025-26), cheap wideband MANET and edge compute only now make transport-agnostic, software-defined tactical networks realistic; NGC2's four-layer stack is 2025-2026 vintage.
Real networks mix SECRET and SBU enclaves, coalition partners, legacy SINCGARS/Link 16 and commercial IP; no single vendor sees or controls all of it.

Pure tactical-network software has a small buyer set; dual-use (public safety, mining, energy, autonomy) exists for radios (Rajant, Silvus) but less for military PACE/NetOps tooling, limiting venture appetite.
Real jamming performance, spectrum plans and Overmatch/MILNET architectures are classified; startups build against sanitized proxies.

attractiveness.bull: The Army has committed roughly $3.3B through FY2026 to C2 Fix/NGC2 and is explicitly buying a 'transport-agnostic' stack that needs software to orchestrate mesh, LEO and 5G; UNO/TNO is moving to a fieldable MVP and an IDIQ; Space Force is spending billions on a LEO backbone whose tactical edge integration is unsolved; DIU's ORIENT problem (mesh-to-long-haul bridging for swarms) drew 130 proposals, proving demand; Silvus's $4.4B+ exit shows this layer generates real M&A outcomes; software layers can be prototyped with COTS gear for under $500k.
attractiveness.bear: Radios are closed to a two-person team; the software layer is being contested by Anduril (now NGC2 data-layer lead), Aalyria, Persistent (Cloud Relay), Motorola/Silvus and RII/CodeMettle, all with head starts and cleared staff; everything of value requires ITAR/CUI access and eventually SECRET clearances, which collides with the non-U.S.-person founder; sales cycles run through OTAs and exercises measured in years; DIU HSA has been in prototype since 2022 with a pilot only in 2026 (purgatory signal); SpaceX's vertical integration removes much of the SATCOM software opportunity.
attractiveness.verdict: Medium attractiveness for a software-only wedge (NetOps/automated PACE, DDIL data movement, gateway translation) sold as a subcontractor into NGC2/UNO teams; low attractiveness for hardware/RF plays; the founder immigration/ITAR profile is the single biggest structural risk and should be legally scoped before any pursuit.

market_stage.rationale: The sequence RFI -> OTA prototype -> follow-on award -> announced FY27 production for NGC2, plus a $13B services vehicle and a $2.29B backbone award in space, shows the segment crossing from prototyping into production. However, GAO flags missing life-cycle costs, and startup-facing DIU efforts remain in pilot, so 'Transitioning' rather than 'Mature'.

proto_purgatory.notes: Program-level purgatory is low: NGC2 moved from OTA prototypes (2025) to an $87.5M follow-on and an FY27 production plan within ~18 months. Startup-level purgatory is visible: DIU HSA awards in July 2022 reached only a 2026 pilot; UNO has iterated RFI (2024) -> OTA Phase I/II (2025) with IDIQ awards 'planned early 2026' unconfirmed; Aalyria has accumulated HSA and ORIENT prototypes without a disclosed production program; Fuse Integration's last verifiable milestone is a 2022 IDIQ seat.
proto_purgatory.opportunity_or_warning: Warning for space/orchestration startups selling to DIU alone; opportunity for teams that attach to an NGC2 or UNO prime already headed to production, because those vehicles now have a fielding date and budget scrutiny (GAO) that favors delivered software over more pilots.

candidate_gaps.title: Vendor-agnostic automated PACE / multi-path transport orchestration at brigade and below
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Units carry three to five transports (MANET, Starlink/pLEO, GEO, 5G, HF) but path selection and failover are still planned on paper and executed by signal soldiers, so applications stall during jamming or movement.
candidate_gaps.user: S6/G6 NetOps cells and platform crews at brigade and below; NGC2 transport-layer integrators
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) S6 writes PACE plan in a spreadsheet/OPORD annex; 2) each radio/terminal configured in its own vendor tool; 3) link degrades; 4) soldier notices via user complaints; 5) manual switch to alternate transport, re-key, re-address; 6) apps re-sync or data is re-entered.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Vendor-specific tools (Silvus Spectrum Dominance, Persistent Cloud Relay), Aalyria Spacetime (prototype), Anduril Lattice Mesh, Navy Overmatch SDN (classified), manual PACE.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: No cross-vendor, policy-driven controller that sees all transports and moves flows automatically; each fix is single-vendor and re-introduces lock-in.

evidence.claim: C2 Fix/NGC2 exist because the tactical network was too complex to 'actually work'; NGC2 differs from C2 Fix in the data and transport layer
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: DIU ORIENT seeks software to connect long-haul comms to local mesh so systems keep operating in disrupted, low-bandwidth environments; 130 proposals received
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: ACC AMIC RFI for readily deployable tactical communications in contested forward environments
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Army has identified ~$3.3B of NGC2 costs through FY2026 and plans division production ecosystem FY27
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: Multiple companies (Aalyria, Persistent Cloud Relay, Anduril, Silvus) attempt partial solutions; none is a cross-vendor production program
evidence.label: INFERENCE

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: Radio vendors guard management APIs; testing requires export-controlled radios and exercise slots; buyers prefer the NGC2 prime to own orchestration; security accreditation of a controller in the encrypted path is slow.
candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: High - Anduril leads NGC2 data layer and can bundle orchestration; Motorola/Silvus and Persistent can extend proprietary controllers.
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: An open, radio-agnostic transport controller (policy engine + per-flow path selection + link quality telemetry) that runs on the existing edge box, speaks each radio's SNMP/REST API, and exposes a simple PACE-as-code interface; sell as a component to NGC2/UNO teams rather than a standalone program.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Linux appliance/container with adapters for Silvus, MPU5, Starlink and a 5G CPE; measures latency/loss/jitter per link; applies PACE policy; demonstrated with 8-10 nodes and induced jamming in a field test; TAK/CoT traffic as the app.
candidate_gaps.data_requirement: Radio telemetry APIs (some ITAR), unclassified link performance data, realistic traffic profiles.
candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: Radio management APIs, Starlink management, IPsec/HAIPE placement, NGC2 integration layer conventions.
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: Army SBIR/xTech, DIU CSO (ORIENT follow-on), subcontract to an NGC2 or UNO IDIQ prime, C5ISR NetModX participation.
candidate_gaps.why_now: NGC2 codified a distinct transport layer and is moving to FY27 production; pLEO plus MANET plus 5G are all fielded, creating the multi-path problem for the first time at scale.
candidate_gaps.killer_risk: Radio vendors close APIs or the NGC2 prime builds it in-house; founders cannot access ITAR technical data due to non-U.S.-person status.

candidate_gaps.title: Single-pane tactical NetOps and spectrum-aware monitoring for S6/G6 in DDIL conditions
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Signal staffs manage the tactical network through many vendor tools that do not share data, so awareness of link health, spectrum conflicts and cyber events is manual and slow.
candidate_gaps.user: Brigade S6 and division G6 NetOps cells; NETCOM
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Open Silvus, Persistent, SATCOM, router and crypto consoles separately; 2) collect status by radio call or chat; 3) transcribe into PowerPoint/Excel network status; 4) deconflict spectrum with S2/EW manually; 5) re-plan and push configs one tool at a time.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: UNO/TNO prototype (RII prime, CodeMettle sub), legacy Army network management tools, vendor consoles.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Consolidation exists only as a prototype; Army's own program goal is to cut the number of tools; UNO IDIQ awards planned early 2026 not yet verified.

evidence.claim: UNO goal is to simplify and reduce the number of network management tools S6/G6 use and ease Signal Soldier workload
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.claim: PEO C3T expected UNO IDIQ RFP early 2025 and awards early 2026 after OTA prototypes
evidence.label: FACT

evidence.label: FACT

candidate_gaps.why_startups_havent_solved: Buyer is a single Army program office with a chosen prototype team; requires SECRET-level integration and NIPR/SIPR ATOs; commercial NetOps vendors lack tactical radio adapters and DDIL tolerance.
candidate_gaps.incumbent_response_risk: High within UNO; medium for USMC/SOCOM/AF niches.
candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: DDIL-tolerant telemetry collector and spectrum overlay (radio RSSI/SNR + EW sensing) feeding an offline-capable dashboard with automated status reporting; plug into TNO via APIs rather than replace it.
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: Edge collector for 3-4 radio types plus Starlink, storing time-series locally and syncing when connected; web HMI on the S6 laptop; auto-generated network status slide.
candidate_gaps.data_requirement: Radio telemetry, spectrum plans (CUI), exercise data.
candidate_gaps.entry_vehicle: Subcontract to UNO IDIQ awardee; SBIR Phase I/II via PEO C3N; USMC/SOCOM pilots.
candidate_gaps.why_now: UNO moving from prototype to IDIQ; NGC2 adds new transports that legacy tools do not cover.
candidate_gaps.killer_risk: UNO primes absorb the function; Army standardizes on RII/CodeMettle stack.

candidate_gaps.title: DDIL-tolerant data movement (store-and-forward, prioritized sync, compression) between edge apps and NGC2 data layer
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: NGC2 apps assume a data layer that stays coherent, but tactical links are intermittent and thin, so edge nodes need prioritized, bandwidth-aware sync that today is bespoke per application.
candidate_gaps.user: NGC2 application developers, fires/logistics cells, Air Force expeditionary units
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) App writes to local DB; 2) link drops; 3) updates queue or are lost; 4) on reconnect, full re-sync floods the link; 5) operators re-enter data or reconcile duplicates.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: Ditto (AFLCMC $28M ceiling), Anduril/Palantir edge sync, TAK Server federation, custom scripts.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: No Army-standard DDIL sync primitive in the NGC2 common data layer baseline is publicly documented; prioritization by mission relevance is immature.

candidate_gaps.technical_wedge_hypothesis: Mission-aware prioritization and delta compression layer between apps and any sync engine, tuned to MANET/LEO link telemetry (bridges G1 and data layer).
candidate_gaps.mvp_sketch: SDK + sidecar that scores messages by mission relevance and link budget; demo with TAK and a logistics app over throttled Silvus/Starlink links.

candidate_gaps.integration_requirement: NGC2 data layer APIs (Anduril-led baseline), TAK.

candidate_gaps.killer_risk: Becomes a feature of Ditto/Lattice; commoditized.

candidate_gaps.title: Software gateway/translation between commercial mesh, TAK and legacy tactical data links (Link 16/VMF) for small units and drones
candidate_gaps.problem_one_sentence: Small units and Replicator-class drones on commercial MANET cannot exchange tracks with Link 16/VMF-based fires and air C2 without an airborne gateway or manual relay.
candidate_gaps.user: Fires cells, JTACs, drone operators, air battle managers
candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Drone track visible in TAK; 2) operator voices grid to fires/air C2; 3) fires re-enters into AFATDS/Link 16 network; 4) latency and transcription errors.
candidate_gaps.current_solution: BACN (aircraft), Viasat BATS-D handheld Link 16, Collins/Fuse gateways, NGC2 integration layer.
candidate_gaps.failure_point: Gateways are hardware-bound, expensive and scarce; software translation requires certified Link 16 access and crypto.

candidate_gaps.current_workflow: 1) Order pLEO via task order; 2) field Starshield terminals; 3) manage through provider portal; 4) alternate providers require separate kits and accounts.
